question_en:
For a vocational school materials class, students are asked to assemble a set of micrographs into a complete cross-section. The teacher only has the attached image. Please use clues in it to search for the full public dataset it belongs to, then answer the following questions:

1. What is the formal name of this dataset, what material is the sample, and how many images are there in total?
2. Examine each image in the full set one by one to find those that simultaneously show a blue polished steel region and a continuous dark external or mounting region. For both regions, measure perpendicularly inward from any image edge they touch; a region qualifies only if it extends continuously to an inset line located at 10% of the image's short side length from that edge. If a region touches multiple edges, meeting the condition on any single edge is sufficient. Scattered black pits, scratches, and narrow edges that do not reach the 10% inset line are not counted. Which image numbers meet all criteria? After merging consecutive numbers into ranges, how many qualifying images are there in total?

Answer Format: Please answer point by point using labels (1)–(2); answer both questions in text. For question 1, provide the name, material, and total number of images. For question 2, merge all qualifying numbers into continuous ranges and provide the total count of qualifying images.
answer:
(1) Formal Name: Differential interference contrast microscopy from a cross section of a fractured ASTM 1008 steel; Sample Material: Cross-section of a fractured ASTM 1008 steel sample; Total Images: 42.

(2) Qualifying numbers merged into ranges: s_001–s_006, s_008–s_010, s_021–s_023, s_032–s_035, s_038–s_042; Total qualifying images: 21.

# Detailed Simulated Retrieval Trajectory · P2-8-3-E01

## Step 01 · Establish Retrieval Entry from Micrograph Texture

Action: Observe the blue polished surface, horizontal texture, and diagonal deep scratches crossing the image in the attachment. Combine these with the background context of assembling micrographs mentioned in the question to query: "blue steel differential interference contrast microscopy image stitching dataset".

Evidence Observation: The current attachment itself contains no institution name, filename, or the total count of 42 images; the steel grade cannot be determined solely from the blue color. First, use the combination of microscopy method, material, and stitching dataset to identify candidates, then compare them with the original image.

Evidence Links:
https://data.nist.gov/od/id/mds2-3676

Result of this step: Obtained a candidate dataset of stitched images of fractured steel cross-sections from NIST.

## Step 02 · Confirm the Same Dataset in Official Records

Action: Open the NIST record, read the title, description, DOI, and record identifier, then compare the scratch position in the attachment with candidate s_014.

Evidence Observation: Record number ark:/88434/mds2-3676, DOI 10.18434/mds2-3676; the attachment corresponds to s_014.tif. The formal title is "Differential interference contrast microscopy from a cross section of a fractured ASTM 1008 steel", and the sample is a cross-section of fractured ASTM 1008 steel.

Evidence Links:
https://data.nist.gov/od/id/mds2-3676
https://doi.org/10.18434/mds2-3676
https://data.nist.gov/od/ds/ark:/88434/mds2-3676/s_014.tif

Result of this step: Identity confirmed by the record and the relationship with the same image; the file number is the retrieval result.

## Step 03 · Establish the Complete Image Set

Action: Read the components list, select only the original image items with type image/tiff, and sort by filepath; list verification files separately and do not count them as images.

Evidence Observation: The description states that 42 images come from a single sample and can be used for image stitching; the original images are consecutively numbered s_001.tif to s_042.tif. Each has a corresponding .sha256 file; verification texts are not additional micrographs, so the two types of components cannot be summed to 84 images.

Evidence Links:
https://data.nist.gov/od/id/mds2-3676
https://data.nist.gov/od/ds/ark:/88434/mds2-3676/

Result of this step: Locked onto 42 original images; no edge images were pre-filtered based on resemblance to the attachment in subsequent steps.

## Step 04 · Verify Original Dimensions and Judgment Distance

Action: Use the short side in the original image's inherent pixel coordinates; do not calculate based on the browser thumbnail width.

Evidence Observation: Original image dimensions are 1360×1024, with a short side of 1024; the 10% inset distance is 102.4 pixels. For the blue steel region and the continuous dark external/mounting region, identify an image edge that each touches; each must continuously extend to the 102.4-pixel inset line from that edge. The two regions may use different edges.

Evidence Links:
https://data.nist.gov/od/ds/ark:/88434/mds2-3676/s_006.tif
https://data.nist.gov/od/ds/ark:/88434/mds2-3676/s_023.tif

Result of this step: Converted the natural language conditions of the question into two verifiable judgments per image.

## Step 05 · Distinguish External Dark Regions from Internal Defects

Action: First review the entry image s_014 and images with scratches to establish negative example criteria, then traverse all files.

Evidence Observation: NIST explains that DIC illumination produces color gradients, and deep scratches may appear in different positions depending on illumination. Isolated black pits, fine scratches, and narrow edges cannot automatically be considered external mounting regions; the entry image s_014 is an internal steel region and does not qualify itself.

Evidence Links:
https://data.nist.gov/od/id/mds2-3676
https://data.nist.gov/od/ds/ark:/88434/mds2-3676/s_014.tif
https://data.nist.gov/od/ds/ark:/88434/mds2-3676/s_029.tif

Result of this step: The per-image check focuses on two types of continuous edge regions, not simply calculating the ratio of blue/black pixels.

Evidence Observation: Both the blue steel and the continuous dark external region exist; both can continuously extend from at least one edge they touch to the 10% inset line.
